title: Super-califragilisticexpialidocious-resolution microscopy: How expansion microscopy can be applied to plants
content: Thanks to the optical resolution of Robert Hooke's handmade compound microscope, he could distinguish the individual plant cells that make up cork. Today, super-resolution imaging beyond Robert Hooke's wildest dreams is made possible with high-end microscopes and techniques like stimulated emission depletion, structured illumination microscopy, and reversible saturable optical linear fluorescence transitions that provide resolution better than the diffraction limit of optical microscopy. Yet, many microscopic structures within and around cells remain challenging to image due to the unfavorable optical properties of plant tissues (Colin et al. 2022). Since its breakthrough discovery almost 10 years ago, expansion microscopy (ExM) offers microscopists the ability to observe their samples at super-resolution with more traditional confocal imaging by expanding their samples on a gel-like matrix (Chen et al. 2015). For plant cells, however, the rigid plant cell wall poses challenges to performing ExM. Now, Michelle Gallei, Sven Truckenbrodt, and colleagues (Gallei et al. 2024) present an approach called PlantEx to achieve super-resolution ExM in Arabidopsis roots.
